To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cTnT, TnC, and cTnI form binary and ternary complexes in blood, with TnC-cTnI being the most abundant complex.
the predominant cTnI circulating form in blood is cTnI complexed to TnC, and that the cTn-I-TnC binary complexes are not affected by the presence of cTnT. This finding is essential for
cTnT, cTnI and TnC are present in the blood of AMI patients and patients undergoing cardiac surgery, and that the predominant cTnI form is the binary complex cTnI–TnC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new cTnI immunoassays and with a better understanding of the cTn isoforms circulating in blood.
the development and validation of a new immunoassay for the measurement of cardiac troponins in the serum of patients with acute coronary syndrome and patients with cardiac surgery.
the development of new assays for the detection of cTnI forms in blood and with the determination of the cTn forms circulating in patients with AMI and during heart surgery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the predominant circulating form in the blood is the IC, which is the most stable and long-lived complex, followed by the free cTnI form.
the predominant circulating form of cTnI in blood is the binary complex cTnI bound to TnC, with a minor contribution of the ternary complex cTnT bound to cTnI and TnC, and the free cTnI form.
the predominant circulating form of cardiac troponins is the binary complex IC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in patients with AMI and in patients receiving cardioplegic solution during heart surgery, cTnI is predominantly present in the binary complex with TnC.
the predominant form of circulating cTnI is the cTninTnC complex.
cTnT, TnC, and cTnI are present in the blood of AMI patients in three different forms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cTnT is not a good primary calibrator for cTnI immunoassays because the cTnC component is not present in the cTnTI-cTnT complex.
the cTnC mAb is a good alternative for the detection of the cTnIC complex.
the use of a primary calibrator that is a cTnI binary complex will provide a higher clinical sensitivity compared to the use of a calibrator that is free cTnI or a ternary complex.
